ARTICLE III: MEMBERSHIP

3.1 Eligibility: Any person who is a resident of the area of operation, whether as an owner,
tenant, or a member of the family of an owner or tenant, and who has attained the age of 18
years, shall be eligible for membership of the Association. For the purpose of this clause, a
"resident" is a person who ordinarily resides in the area of operation for at least six months in a
calendar year.

3.2 Application for Membership: Application for membership shall be made in the prescribed form
to the Secretary. The application shall be accompanied by proof of residence (such as a copy of
a utility bill, rental agreement, or Aadhaar card) and the annual membership fee as determined
by the General Body from time to time.

3.3 Admission: The Executive Committee shall consider all applications for membership and shall
have the power to admit or reject any application. The decision of the Executive Committee shall
be final and binding. However, no application shall be rejected without recording the reasons
therefor in writing.

3.4 Types of Membership:
(a) Ordinary Member: Any eligible resident who pays the prescribed annual subscription.
(b) Life Member: Any eligible resident who pays a one-time subscription as fixed by the
General Body. Life Members shall have all the rights and privileges of Ordinary Members
and shall not be required to pay the annual subscription.
(c) Honorary Member: The Executive Committee may, by a majority resolution, confer
Honorary Membership on any person who has rendered distinguished service to the
Association or to the community. Honorary Members shall have the right to attend
meetings but shall not have the right to vote or hold office.

3.5 Cessation of Membership: Membership shall cease upon:
(a) Written resignation tendered to the Secretary.
(b) Non-payment of the annual subscription for two consecutive years, provided that a
notice of arrears has been sent to the member at least thirty days prior to the cessation.
(c) Death.
(d) Ceasing to be a resident of the area of operation for a continuous period of twelve
months.
(e) Expulsion by the General Body for conduct detrimental to the interests of the
Association, provided that the member is given an opportunity to be heard.

3.6 Register of Members: The Secretary shall maintain a Register of Members containing the name,
address, contact number, email address, and date of admission of each member. The Register
shall be open for inspection by any member at the registered office during reasonable hours.
Provided that no office bearer shall hold the same office for more than two consecutive terms. A person who has held the office of President for two consecutive terms shall not be eligible for re-election to the same office until the lapse of one full term. This restriction shall not apply to Ordinary Members of the Executive Committee.

4.4 **Vacancies**: In the event of a vacancy arising in the Executive Committee due to resignation, death, disqualification, or removal, the Executive Committee shall have the power to co-opt a member to fill the vacancy. Such co-opted member shall hold office only until the next AGM and shall have all the rights and privileges of a member of the Executive Committee.

4.5 **Resignation**: Any office bearer or member of the Executive Committee may resign by tendering a written resignation to the Secretary. The resignation shall take effect from the date of its acceptance by the Executive Committee or from the date specified in the resignation, whichever is later.

4.6 **Removal**: The General Body may, by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting at a specially convened meeting, remove any office bearer or member of the Executive Committee before the expiry of their term for:
(a) Non-performance of duties;
(b) Misconduct;
(c) Acts detrimental to the interests of the Association.

Provided that the person concerned shall be given an opportunity to present their case before the General Body.

4.7 **Powers and Duties of the Executive Committee**: The Executive Committee shall have the following powers and duties:
(a) To manage the day-to-day affairs of the Association;
(b) To implement the resolutions of the General Body;
(c) To open and operate bank accounts in the name of the Association;
(d) To appoint, remove, and fix the remuneration of employees of the Association;
(e) To prepare and present the annual budget and audited accounts at the AGM;
(f) To enter into contracts and agreements on behalf of the Association;
(g) To appoint sub-committees for specific purposes and to delegate such powers as may be necessary.

4.8 **Meetings of the Executive Committee**: The Executive Committee shall meet at least once every two months. The Secretary shall convene the meeting by giving not less than seven days' notice in writing to all members of the Committee. The quorum for a meeting of the Executive Committee shall be one-third of the total membership or five members, whichever is less.

**ARTICLE 5: OFFICE BEARERS – SPECIFIC ROLES**

5.1 **President**: The President shall preside over all meetings of the General Body and the Executive Committee. The President shall have a casting vote in the event of a tie. The President shall also be the official spokesperson of the Association.

5.2 **Vice-President**: The Vice-President shall perform the duties of the President in the latter's absence and shall assist the President in the discharge of their duties.

5.3 **Secretary**: The Secretary shall be responsible for:
(a) Maintaining the minutes of all meetings of the General Body and the Executive Committee;
(b) Maintaining the Register of Members;
(c) Issuing notices for meetings;
(d) Conducting correspondence on behalf of the Association;
(e) Maintaining custody of the records and documents of the Association, other than the financial records.

5.4 **Joint Secretary**: The Joint Secretary shall assist the Secretary in the discharge of their duties and shall perform the duties of the Secretary in the latter's absence.
6.3 **Application for Membership**: Application for membership shall be made in the prescribed form, accompanied by the prescribed subscription for the relevant category. The application shall be considered by the Executive Committee at its next meeting, and the decision of the Committee shall be communicated to the applicant within fifteen days thereof.

6.4 **Register of Members**: The Secretary shall maintain a Register of Members in which shall be recorded, in respect of each member: name, address, contact number, email address, category of membership, date of admission, and the membership status. The membership status shall be recorded as "active" or "suspended" or "terminated" as the case may be. The Register of Members shall be open to inspection by any member at reasonable hours, upon prior appointment with the Secretary.

6.5 **Rights of Members**: Every active member shall have the right to:
(a) Attend and vote at all meetings of the General Body;
(b) Propose or second candidates for election to the Executive Committee, subject to Article 7;
(c) Receive notices and minutes of meetings;
(d) Inspect the books of account and records as provided under these Byelaws.

6.6 **Cessation of Membership**: Membership shall cease upon:
(a) Written resignation, effective from the date of receipt by the Secretary;
(b) Death;
(c) Termination by the Executive Committee for conduct prejudicial to the interests of the Association, provided that the member shall be given an opportunity of being heard;
(d) Non-payment of subscription for a continuous period of twelve months, provided that notice of arrears has been served on the member at least two months prior to such cessation.

6.7 **Re-admission**: A person whose membership has ceased under clause 6.6(d) may apply for re-admission under clause 6.3, and the Executive Committee may, in its discretion, admit such person on payment of the arrears and the current subscription.

6.8 **Subscriptions**: The annual subscription shall be fixed by the General Body from time to time. The subscription shall be payable on or before the 30th of April of each year. Members admitted during the course of the year shall pay the full annual subscription.

**ARTICLE 7: ELECTIONS**

7.1 **Election Committee**: The outgoing Executive Committee shall appoint an Election Committee, comprising of three members who are not candidates for election, to conduct the elections in a fair and transparent manner.

7.2 **Nomination**: Nominations shall be called by the Election Committee by public notice, not less than twenty-one days prior to the date of the Annual General Meeting. Every nomination shall be in writing, proposed by one member and seconded by another, and the consent of the nominee shall be obtained in writing.

7.3 **Election Procedure**: If the number of valid nominations exceeds the number of vacancies, an election shall be held by secret ballot at the Annual General Meeting. If the number of valid nominations equals the number of vacancies, the nominees shall be declared elected without a ballot.

7.4 **Casting Vote**: In the event of a tie in any election, the Chairperson of the meeting shall have a casting vote.

7.5 **Election to Office Bearers**: The office bearers shall be elected by the members of the Executive Committee from amongst themselves, at the first meeting of the newly constituted Committee.
**ARTICLE 8: MAINTENANCE FEES AND OTHER CHARGES**

8.1 **Levy of Maintenance Fees**: The Executive Committee shall have the power to levy, revise, or
re-structure the maintenance fees payable by members in respect of their respective premises or
plots, as the case may be. Every such levy or revision shall be effected only by a resolution of
the Executive Committee passed at a duly convened meeting, and such resolution shall thereafter be
placed before the members for ratification.

8.2 **General Body Approval**: No revision of maintenance fees shall take effect unless it has been
approved by a majority of the members present and voting at a General Body Meeting duly convened for
that purpose. The notice for such meeting shall specify, in clear terms, the proposed revision and
the date from which it is intended to take effect. Approval by show of hands or by ballot, as the
meeting may decide, shall be deemed to be the approval of the members for the purpose of this
clause.

8.3 **Binding Nature**: Every revision of maintenance fees, once approved in the manner set out in
clauses 8.1 and 8.2 above, shall be binding on all members, whether or not such member was present
at, or voted in favour of, the resolution at the General Body Meeting. A copy of the resolution
shall be circulated to all members within fifteen days of the meeting, and such circulation shall be
sufficient notice of the revised fees.

8.4 **Frequency of Revision**: Nothing in this Article shall require the Executive Committee to
revise the maintenance fees at any fixed interval. Revisions may be made as and when the financial
position of the Association so requires, subject to the procedure prescribed herein.

8.5 **Special Assessment**: In addition to the regular maintenance fees, the Executive Committee
may, by resolution and with the approval of the General Body as aforesaid, levy a special assessment
for a specific purpose, such as major repairs, legal expenses, or capital improvements. The special
assessment shall be collected in such instalments and within such time as the resolution may
specify.

8.6 **Interest on Arrears**: Maintenance fees and special assessments remaining unpaid after the
due date shall carry interest at the rate of eighteen percent per annum, or such other rate as may
be fixed by the Executive Committee from time to time, not exceeding twenty-four percent per annum.
The levy of interest shall not be construed as a waiver of the Association's right to take action
under clause 6.6 of these Bylaws.

8.7 **Recovery of Arrears**: Without prejudice to any other remedy available to the Association,
the Executive Committee may recover arrears of maintenance fees, special assessments, and interest
thereon by withholding services provided by the Association, including but not limited to
maintenance of common areas, access to common facilities, and issue of no-objection certificates.

**ARTICLE 9: GENERAL BODY MEETINGS**

9.1 **Annual General Meeting**: The Annual General Meeting of the Association shall be held once in
every calendar year, within six months of the close of the financial year, at such date, time, and
place as the Executive Committee may determine.

9.2 **Business of the Annual General Meeting**: The business of the Annual General Meeting shall
include:
(a) Confirmation of the minutes of the previous General Body Meeting;
(b) Consideration and adoption of the audited accounts for the preceding financial year;
(c) Consideration and adoption of the budget for the current financial year;
(d) Consideration of the report of the Executive Committee on the activities of the Association;
(e) Election of the Executive Committee, where applicable;
(f) Any other business brought before the meeting with the permission of the Chairperson.
**ARTICLE 10: RESIGNATION AND REMOVAL OF OFFICE BEARERS**

10.1 **Resignation of Office Bearers**: Any office bearer of the Association may resign from
his or her office by tendering a resignation in writing addressed to the Secretary, or to the
President, or, in the absence of both, to the Executive Committee. The resignation shall take
effect immediately upon receipt by the Association, and no acceptance by the Executive Committee
shall be necessary to make the resignation valid. The receipt of the resignation shall be noted
in the minutes of the next meeting of the Executive Committee, and the date of receipt shall be
recorded in the register of resignations maintained by the Secretary.

10.2 **Vice-President to Assume Role**: Upon the resignation of the President, the
Vice-President shall assume the office of President for the remainder of the term. In the event
of the resignation of the Vice-President, the Executive Committee may appoint one of its members
to fill the vacancy for the remainder of the term, or may co-opt a member of the Association to
the Executive Committee for this purpose. The office bearer so appointed or co-opted shall hold
office until the next Annual General Meeting.

10.3 **Resignation of Other Office Bearers**: The resignation of the Secretary, Treasurer, or
any other office bearer shall be effective immediately upon receipt, and the Executive Committee
shall make arrangements for the discharge of the duties of the office by one of its members or by
a co-opted member until a successor is elected or appointed.

10.4 **Removal from Office**: The Executive Committee may, by a resolution passed by a majority
of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting at a meeting of the Executive
Committee, remove any office bearer from office for:
(a) failure to discharge the duties of the office;
(b) breach of the provisions of the Constitution or these Bylaws;
(c) misappropriation of the funds of the Association; or
(d) conduct which brings the Association into disrepute.
The office bearer concerned shall be given an opportunity to be heard before any such resolution
is passed.

10.5 **Vacancies**: Any vacancy in the office of the President, Vice-President, Secretary,
Treasurer, or any other office bearer shall be filled in accordance with the provisions of this
Article, and the person so appointed shall hold office for the remainder of the term of the
office bearer whose vacancy is so filled.

**ARTICLE 11: ELECTIONS**

11.1 **Election Committee**: The Executive Committee shall, at least sixty days before the date
of the Annual General Meeting at which elections are to be held, appoint an Election Committee
consisting of three members of the Association who are not members of the Executive Committee and
who are not candidates for election. The Election Committee shall conduct the elections in a fair
and transparent manner.

11.2 **Notice of Elections**: The Election Committee shall issue a notice of elections at least
thirty days before the date of the Annual General Meeting, inviting nominations for the offices
of President, Vice-President, Secretary, Treasurer, and such other offices as may be created by
the Executive Committee.

11.3 **Nominations**: Any member of the Association may nominate himself or herself for any
office, provided the nomination is proposed and seconded by two other members in good standing.
No member may contest for more than one office in the same election.
**ARTICLE 12: FINANCE AND ACCOUNTS**

12.1 **Financial Year**: The financial year of the Association shall commence on the 1st day of April and end on the 31st day of March of the following year.

12.2 **Maintenance of Funds**: The Association shall maintain the following funds:
(a) General Fund;
(b) Corpus Fund; and
(c) such other special funds as the Executive Committee may, from time to time, create for specific purposes.

12.3 **General Fund**: All membership fees, admission fees, donations, grants, and other receipts of the Association, not specifically earmarked for any other fund, shall be credited to the General Fund. All expenses of the Association shall be met from the General Fund.

12.4 **Corpus Fund**: The Corpus Fund shall consist of amounts transferred from the General Fund by resolution of the Executive Committee, and any donations or grants specifically made to the Corpus Fund. The Corpus Fund shall be utilised only for capital expenditure or for such purposes as may be decided by the General Body, and shall not be utilised for routine maintenance or administrative expenses.

12.5 **Special Funds**: Where the Executive Committee creates a special fund for a specific purpose, the terms and conditions governing such fund shall be recorded in a resolution of the Executive Committee, and the fund shall be operated in accordance with those terms.

12.6 **Bank Accounts**: The funds of the Association shall be kept in a bank account or accounts in the name of the Association. The bank accounts shall be operated jointly by the Treasurer and either the President or the Secretary. No payment shall be made from the funds of the Association except by cheque or electronic transfer, supported by a bill or voucher duly approved by the Treasurer and countersigned by the President or the Secretary.

12.7 **Authorisation of Expenditure**: All expenditure from the General Fund shall be authorised by the Executive Committee. The Executive Committee may delegate to the President and the Treasurer the power to sanction routine expenditure up to an amount of ₹10,000 (Rupees Ten Thousand only) per transaction, provided that the total of such delegated expenditure between two consecutive Executive Committee meetings shall not exceed ₹50,000 (Rupees Fifty Thousand only). Any expenditure exceeding the said limits shall require the prior approval of the Executive Committee.

12.8 **Prohibition on Loans**: No loan shall be made by the Association to any member, office bearer, or employee of the Association. No part of the funds of the Association shall be applied, directly or indirectly, for the benefit of any member, office bearer, or employee, except as provided in this Article.

12.9 **Financial Reporting**: The Treasurer shall present a financial report at every meeting of the Executive Committee, showing the receipts and payments during the period since the last report, and the balance in each fund of the Association. A copy of the financial report shall be made available to any member of the Association upon request.

12.10 **Annual Accounts**: The Treasurer shall, at the close of each financial year, prepare the annual accounts of the Association, including the income and expenditure account and the balance sheet, and shall submit the same to the Auditors for audit.

12.11 **Audit**: The accounts of the Association shall be audited at the close of each financial year by an auditor appointed by the General Body at the Annual General Meeting. The auditor shall not be a member of the Executive Committee. The auditor shall examine the accounts and shall submit a report to the Association, stating whether the accounts present a true and fair view of the financial position of the Association. The audited accounts and the auditor's report shall be presented to the members at the Annual General Meeting.
ARTICLE 13 — AMENDMENT OF THE CONSTITUTION

13.1 **Power to Amend**: The General Body of the Association shall have the power to alter, amend, add to, or repeal any provision of this Constitution, subject to the provisions of this Article.

13.2 **Procedure for Amendment**: Any proposed amendment to this Constitution shall be made in writing and shall be signed by at least twenty (20) members of the Association who are entitled to vote. The proposed amendment shall be submitted to the Secretary at least thirty (30) days prior to the date fixed for the meeting of the General Body at which the amendment is to be considered.

13.3 **Notice of Amendment**: Upon receipt of a proposed amendment, the Secretary shall cause a copy of the proposed amendment to be circulated to all members of the Association along with the notice convening the General Body meeting, not less than fourteen (14) days before the date of such meeting. The notice shall state the text of the proposed amendment and the names of the members proposing the same.

13.4 **Consideration and Adoption**: No amendment to this Constitution shall be effective unless it is approved by a majority of not less than two-thirds (2/3) of the members present and voting at a duly convened meeting of the General Body. Voting on any amendment shall be by show of hands or by secret ballot, as the Chairperson may decide, provided that if not less than ten (10) members present demand a secret ballot, the same shall be held.

13.5 **No Retrospective Effect**: No amendment made under this Article shall have retrospective effect so as to invalidate any act done, or any decision taken, in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution prior to the date of such amendment.

13.6 **Amendments to be Recorded**: Every amendment made under this Article shall be numbered serially, recorded in a register maintained for the purpose, and incorporated into the text of this Constitution. The Secretary shall certify the date of adoption of every amendment and shall attach a copy of the certified amendment to the minutes of the meeting at which it was adopted.

13.7 **Bylaws**: The Executive Committee may, from time to time, frame, adopt, amend, or repeal bylaws for the smooth functioning of the Association, provided that such bylaws are not inconsistent with the provisions of this Constitution. All bylaws framed under this clause shall be placed before the General Body for ratification at its next meeting.

ARTICLE 14 — DISPUTE RESOLUTION

14.1 **Aim**: The Association shall endeavour to resolve all disputes arising among members, or between members and the Association, or between the Association and any third party, in an amicable and expeditious manner, with a view to preserving the harmony of the community.

14.2 **Internal Grievance Redressal**: Any member having a grievance against the Association, or against any office bearer or member of the Executive Committee, shall first submit the grievance in writing to the Secretary. The Secretary shall place the grievance before the Executive Committee at its next meeting, and the Executive Committee shall endeavour to resolve the grievance within thirty (30) days of receipt thereof.

14.3 **Grievance Redressal Committee**: If the grievance is not resolved by the Executive Committee within the time specified in clause 14.2, or if the grievance relates to a decision of the Executive Committee, the matter may be referred by the aggrieved member to a Grievance Redressal Committee. The Grievance Redressal Committee shall consist of three (3) members of the Association, not being members of the Executive Committee, nominated by the General Body at its Annual General Meeting. The Grievance Redressal Committee shall hear the parties and shall make its recommendations in writing within thirty (30) days of the reference.

ARTICLE II: AIMS AND OBJECTIVES

2.1 To promote and protect the common interests of the residents of Indiranagar.

lighting, and garbage clearance with the concerned municipal and government authorities.

2.4 To foster a sense of community and organize cultural, social, and welfare activities for the

of Indiranagar.

ARTICLE III: MEMBERSHIP

3.1 Eligibility: Any person who is a resident of the area of operation, whether as an owner,
tenant, or a member of the family of an owner or tenant, and who has attained the age of 18
years, shall be eligible for membership of the Association. For the purpose of this clause, a
"resident" is a person who ordinarily resides in the area of operation for at least six months in a
calendar year.

3.2 Application for Membership: Application for membership shall be made in the prescribed form
to the Secretary. The application shall be accompanied by proof of residence (such as a copy of
a utility bill, rental agreement, or Aadhaar card) and the annual membership fee as determined
by the General Body from time to time.

3.3 Admission: The Executive Committee shall consider all applications for membership and shall
have the power to admit or reject any application. The decision of the Executive Committee shall
be final and binding. However, no application shall be rejected without recording the reasons
therefor in writing.

3.4 Types of Membership:
(a) Ordinary Member: Any eligible resident who pays the prescribed annual subscription.
(b) Life Member: Any eligible resident who pays a one-time subscription as fixed by the
General Body. Life Members shall have all the rights and privileges of Ordinary Members
and shall not be required to pay the annual subscription.
(c) Honorary Member: The Executive Committee may, by a majority resolution, confer
Honorary Membership on any person who has rendered distinguished service to the
Association or to the community. Honorary Members shall have the right to attend
meetings but shall not have the right to vote or hold office.

3.5 Cessation of Membership: Membership shall cease upon:
(a) Written resignation tendered to the Secretary.
(b) Non-payment of the annual subscription for two consecutive years, provided that a
notice of arrears has been sent to the member at least thirty days prior to the cessation.
(c) Death.
(d) Ceasing to be a resident of the area of operation for a continuous period of twelve
months.
(e) Expulsion by the General Body for conduct detrimental to the interests of the
Association, provided that the member is given an opportunity to be heard.

3.6 Register of Members: The Secretary shall maintain a Register of Members containing the name,
address, contact number, email address, and date of admission of each member. The Register
shall be open for inspection by any member at the registered office during reasonable hours.

**ARTICLE 8: MAINTENANCE FEES AND OTHER CHARGES**

8.1 **Levy of Maintenance Fees**: The Executive Committee shall have the power to levy, revise, or
re-structure the maintenance fees payable by members in respect of their respective premises or
plots, as the case may be. Every such levy or revision shall be effected only by a resolution of
the Executive Committee passed at a duly convened meeting, and such resolution shall thereafter be
placed before the members for ratification.

8.2 **General Body Approval**: No revision of maintenance fees shall take effect unless it has been
approved by a majority of the members present and voting at a General Body Meeting duly convened for
that purpose. The notice for such meeting shall specify, in clear terms, the proposed revision and
the date from which it is intended to take effect. Approval by show of hands or by ballot, as the
meeting may decide, shall be deemed to be the approval of the members for the purpose of this
clause.

8.3 **Binding Nature**: Every revision of maintenance fees, once approved in the manner set out in
clauses 8.1 and 8.2 above, shall be binding on all members, whether or not such member was present
at, or voted in favour of, the resolution at the General Body Meeting. A copy of the resolution
shall be circulated to all members within fifteen days of the meeting, and such circulation shall be
sufficient notice of the revised fees.

8.4 **Frequency of Revision**: Nothing in this Article shall require the Executive Committee to
revise the maintenance fees at any fixed interval. Revisions may be made as and when the financial
position of the Association so requires, subject to the procedure prescribed herein.

8.5 **Special Assessment**: In addition to the regular maintenance fees, the Executive Committee
may, by resolution and with the approval of the General Body as aforesaid, levy a special assessment
for a specific purpose, such as major repairs, legal expenses, or capital improvements. The special
assessment shall be collected in such instalments and within such time as the resolution may
specify.

8.6 **Interest on Arrears**: Maintenance fees and special assessments remaining unpaid after the
due date shall carry interest at the rate of eighteen percent per annum, or such other rate as may
be fixed by the Executive Committee from time to time, not exceeding twenty-four percent per annum.
The levy of interest shall not be construed as a waiver of the Association's right to take action
under clause 6.6 of these Bylaws.

8.7 **Recovery of Arrears**: Without prejudice to any other remedy available to the Association,
the Executive Committee may recover arrears of maintenance fees, special assessments, and interest
thereon by withholding services provided by the Association, including but not limited to
maintenance of common areas, access to common facilities, and issue of no-objection certificates.

**ARTICLE 9: GENERAL BODY MEETINGS**

9.1 **Annual General Meeting**: The Annual General Meeting of the Association shall be held once in
every calendar year, within six months of the close of the financial year, at such date, time, and
place as the Executive Committee may determine.

9.2 **Business of the Annual General Meeting**: The business of the Annual General Meeting shall
include:
(a) Confirmation of the minutes of the previous General Body Meeting;
(b) Consideration and adoption of the audited accounts for the preceding financial year;
(c) Consideration and adoption of the budget for the current financial year;
(d) Consideration of the report of the Executive Committee on the activities of the Association;
(e) Election of the Executive Committee, where applicable;
(f) Any other business brought before the meeting with the permission of the Chairperson.

his or her office by tendering a resignation in writing addressed to the Secretary, or to the
President, or, in the absence of both, to the Executive Committee. The resignation shall take
effect immediately upon receipt by the Association, and no acceptance by the Executive Committee
shall be necessary to make the resignation valid. The receipt of the resignation shall be noted
in the minutes of the next meeting of the Executive Committee, and the date of receipt shall be
recorded in the register of resignations maintained by the Secretary.

10.2 **Vice-President to Assume Role**: Upon the resignation of the President, the
Vice-President shall assume the office of President for the remainder of the term. In the event
of the resignation of the Vice-President, the Executive Committee may appoint one of its members
to fill the vacancy for the remainder of the term, or may co-opt a member of the Association to
the Executive Committee for this purpose. The office bearer so appointed or co-opted shall hold
office until the next Annual General Meeting.

10.3 **Resignation of Other Office Bearers**: The resignation of the Secretary, Treasurer, or
any other office bearer shall be effective immediately upon receipt, and the Executive Committee
shall make arrangements for the discharge of the duties of the office by one of its members or by
a co-opted member until a successor is elected or appointed.

10.4 **Removal from Office**: The Executive Committee may, by a resolution passed by a majority
of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting at a meeting of the Executive
Committee, remove any office bearer from office for:
(a) failure to discharge the duties of the office;
(b) breach of the provisions of the Constitution or these Bylaws;
(c) misappropriation of the funds of the Association; or
(d) conduct which brings the Association into disrepute.
The office bearer concerned shall be given an opportunity to be heard before any such resolution
is passed.

10.5 **Vacancies**: Any vacancy in the office of the President, Vice-President, Secretary,
Treasurer, or any other office bearer shall be filled in accordance with the provisions of this
Article, and the person so appointed shall hold office for the remainder of the term of the
office bearer whose vacancy is so filled.

**ARTICLE 11: ELECTIONS**

11.1 **Election Committee**: The Executive Committee shall, at least sixty days before the date
of the Annual General Meeting at which elections are to be held, appoint an Election Committee
consisting of three members of the Association who are not members of the Executive Committee and
who are not candidates for election. The Election Committee shall conduct the elections in a fair
and transparent manner.

11.2 **Notice of Elections**: The Election Committee shall issue a notice of elections at least
thirty days before the date of the Annual General Meeting, inviting nominations for the offices
of President, Vice-President, Secretary, Treasurer, and such other offices as may be created by
the Executive Committee.

11.3 **Nominations**: Any member of the Association may nominate himself or herself for any
office, provided the nomination is proposed and seconded by two other members in good standing.
No member may contest for more than one office in the same election.

documents.content:
**ARTICLE 12: FINANCE AND ACCOUNTS**

12.1 **Financial Year**: The financial year of the Association shall commence on the 1st day of April and end on the 31st day of March of the following year.

12.2 **Maintenance of Funds**: The Association shall maintain the following funds:
(a) General Fund;
(b) Corpus Fund; and
(c) such other special funds as the Executive Committee may, from time to time, create for specific purposes.

12.3 **General Fund**: All membership fees, admission fees, donations, grants, and other receipts of the Association, not specifically earmarked for any other fund, shall be credited to the General Fund. All expenses of the Association shall be met from the General Fund.

12.4 **Corpus Fund**: The Corpus Fund shall consist of amounts transferred from the General Fund by resolution of the Executive Committee, and any donations or grants specifically made to the Corpus Fund. The Corpus Fund shall be utilised only for capital expenditure or for such purposes as may be decided by the General Body, and shall not be utilised for routine maintenance or administrative expenses.

12.5 **Special Funds**: Where the Executive Committee creates a special fund for a specific purpose, the terms and conditions governing such fund shall be recorded in a resolution of the Executive Committee, and the fund shall be operated in accordance with those terms.

12.6 **Bank Accounts**: The funds of the Association shall be kept in a bank account or accounts in the name of the Association. The bank accounts shall be operated jointly by the Treasurer and either the President or the Secretary. No payment shall be made from the funds of the Association except by cheque or electronic transfer, supported by a bill or voucher duly approved by the Treasurer and countersigned by the President or the Secretary.

12.7 **Authorisation of Expenditure**: All expenditure from the General Fund shall be authorised by the Executive Committee. The Executive Committee may delegate to the President and the Treasurer the power to sanction routine expenditure up to an amount of ₹10,000 (Rupees Ten Thousand only) per transaction, provided that the total of such delegated expenditure between two consecutive Executive Committee meetings shall not exceed ₹50,000 (Rupees Fifty Thousand only). Any expenditure exceeding the said limits shall require the prior approval of the Executive Committee.

12.8 **Prohibition on Loans**: No loan shall be made by the Association to any member, office bearer, or employee of the Association. No part of the funds of the Association shall be applied, directly or indirectly, for the benefit of any member, office bearer, or employee, except as provided in this Article.

12.9 **Financial Reporting**: The Treasurer shall present a financial report at every meeting of the Executive Committee, showing the receipts and payments during the period since the last report, and the balance in each fund of the Association. A copy of the financial report shall be made available to any member of the Association upon request.

12.10 **Annual Accounts**: The Treasurer shall, at the close of each financial year, prepare the annual accounts of the Association, including the income and expenditure account and the balance sheet, and shall submit the same to the Auditors for audit.

12.11 **Audit**: The accounts of the Association shall be audited at the close of each financial year by an auditor appointed by the General Body at the Annual General Meeting. The auditor shall not be a member of the Executive Committee. The auditor shall examine the accounts and shall submit a report to the Association, stating whether the accounts present a true and fair view of the financial position of the Association. The audited accounts and the auditor's report shall be presented to the members at the Annual General Meeting.

ARTICLE 13 — AMENDMENT OF THE CONSTITUTION

13.1 **Power to Amend**: The General Body of the Association shall have the power to alter, amend, add to, or repeal any provision of this Constitution, subject to the provisions of this Article.

13.2 **Procedure for Amendment**: Any proposed amendment to this Constitution shall be made in writing and shall be signed by at least twenty (20) members of the Association who are entitled to vote. The proposed amendment shall be submitted to the Secretary at least thirty (30) days prior to the date fixed for the meeting of the General Body at which the amendment is to be considered.

13.3 **Notice of Amendment**: Upon receipt of a proposed amendment, the Secretary shall cause a copy of the proposed amendment to be circulated to all members of the Association along with the notice convening the General Body meeting, not less than fourteen (14) days before the date of such meeting. The notice shall state the text of the proposed amendment and the names of the members proposing the same.

13.4 **Consideration and Adoption**: No amendment to this Constitution shall be effective unless it is approved by a majority of not less than two-thirds (2/3) of the members present and voting at a duly convened meeting of the General Body. Voting on any amendment shall be by show of hands or by secret ballot, as the Chairperson may decide, provided that if not less than ten (10) members present demand a secret ballot, the same shall be held.

13.5 **No Retrospective Effect**: No amendment made under this Article shall have retrospective effect so as to invalidate any act done, or any decision taken, in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution prior to the date of such amendment.

13.6 **Amendments to be Recorded**: Every amendment made under this Article shall be numbered serially, recorded in a register maintained for the purpose, and incorporated into the text of this Constitution. The Secretary shall certify the date of adoption of every amendment and shall attach a copy of the certified amendment to the minutes of the meeting at which it was adopted.

13.7 **Bylaws**: The Executive Committee may, from time to time, frame, adopt, amend, or repeal bylaws for the smooth functioning of the Association, provided that such bylaws are not inconsistent with the provisions of this Constitution. All bylaws framed under this clause shall be placed before the General Body for ratification at its next meeting.

ARTICLE 14 — DISPUTE RESOLUTION

14.1 **Aim**: The Association shall endeavour to resolve all disputes arising among members, or between members and the Association, or between the Association and any third party, in an amicable and expeditious manner, with a view to preserving the harmony of the community.

14.2 **Internal Grievance Redressal**: Any member having a grievance against the Association, or against any office bearer or member of the Executive Committee, shall first submit the grievance in writing to the Secretary. The Secretary shall place the grievance before the Executive Committee at its next meeting, and the Executive Committee shall endeavour to resolve the grievance within thirty (30) days of receipt thereof.

14.3 **Grievance Redressal Committee**: If the grievance is not resolved by the Executive Committee within the time specified in clause 14.2, or if the grievance relates to a decision of the Executive Committee, the matter may be referred by the aggrieved member to a Grievance Redressal Committee. The Grievance Redressal Committee shall consist of three (3) members of the Association, not being members of the Executive Committee, nominated by the General Body at its Annual General Meeting. The Grievance Redressal Committee shall hear the parties and shall make its recommendations in writing within thirty (30) days of the reference.

After discussion, it was resolved that the EC be authorized to engage the services of the tax consultant, M/s R. Gopal & Associates, who had handled the previous appeal, and to file a formal objection with BBMP before the due date of 15 May 2023. The resolution was proposed by Mr. D. S. Prabhu and seconded by Ms. L. Fernandes.

Vote: For – 47, Against – 2, Abstentions – 3. Motion No. 3/2023 was passed by a majority.

16. FEE REVISION PROPOSALS FOR NON-RESIDENTIAL USERS

The outgoing EC had earlier circulated a proposal regarding revision of fees for non-residential users of the community hall and the badminton court. The proposal, dated 28 March 2023, was discussed at length. Some members felt the proposed increase of 15% for hall rental was too steep, while others pointed out that the maintenance costs had risen and that the fees had not been revised since 2019.

After discussion, the following amendments were considered:

- Amendment to reduce hall rental increase from 15% to 10% for the first year. Proposed by Mr. A. K. Nair, seconded by Mr. R. S. Murthy. Vote: For – 29, Against – 21, Abstentions – 2. The amendment was lost.

- Amendment to defer the badminton court fee revision by six months. Proposed by Ms. P. D’Souza, seconded by Mr. V. K. Rao. Vote: For – 12, Against – 38, Abstentions – 2. The amendment was lost.

The original proposal was then put to vote.

Vote: For – 41, Against – 9, Abstentions – 2. Motion No. 4/2023 was passed.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
OBJECTION PROCEDURE – ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------------------------------

In continuation of the objection procedure outlined in the main notice,
the following additional points are brought to the attention of the
assessee:

1. Grounds for objection: An objection may be filed on any of the
   following grounds, supported by documentary evidence:
   (a) Incorrect plinth area or measurement of the building.
   (b) Incorrect classification of usage (e.g., residential vs.
       commercial, self-occupied vs. tenanted).
   (c) Incorrect application of the monthly rent per sq. ft. as per
       the relevant circular.
   (d) Non-application of allowable deductions (repairs, vacancy,
       etc.).
   (e) Any other error in the computation of ARV.

2. Documents required for objection:
   - Copy of this notice.
   - Proof of ownership (sale deed, khata certificate, or registered
     lease deed).
   - Occupancy certificate / building license, if available.
   - Rent agreement for tenanted portions (if any).
   - Any other document supporting the grounds of objection.

3. Mode of filing: Objections may be filed in person at the office of
   the Assistant Revenue Officer, Ward No. 69 (HMT Layout), BBMP East
   Zone Office, between 10:30 AM and 5:00 PM on working days, or sent
   by post to the same address. Online filing is also available through
   the BBMP website (www.bbmp.gov.in) under the "Property Tax –
   Objection" tab, quoting the Notice No. and PID mentioned above.
